scope: Primary-source evidence for U.S. utility and industrial operator education. Status labels deliberately distinguish deployments, pilots, products, and adjacent AI.

cases.title: California ISO + OATI AI Genie
cases.us_relevance: California-based grid operator and Western U.S. reliability coordinator; Minnesota-based software vendor
cases.status: Vendor-reported production deployment; customer-confirmed earlier pilot
cases.slide_claim: CAISO's outage-review assistant combines retrieval and specialized agents. OATI reports production use since June 24, 2026 and nightly analysis of 500+ next-day outage requests in under eight minutes. Reviewers retain final authority.
operator_workflow: Prepare nightly reports and geospatial context
cases.agentic_evidence: CAISO describes RAG combined with a multi-agent framework. OATI describes workflow, advisor, reconnaissance, and autonomous analysis agents coordinated by an orchestrator.
cases.boundary: Evidence concerns outage-data review and decision support. It does not establish autonomous switching, generation dispatch, or independent approval of outages.
cases.metric_caveat: 500+ requests / <8 minutes is reported by vendor OATI, summarizing CAISO field experience. No independent causal evaluation located. Do not conflate it with OATI's separate 15-minute marketing claim.

cases.title: GE Aerospace + Palantir: production readiness
cases.organization: GE Aerospace; Palantir; U.S. Air Force
cases.us_relevance: U.S. industrial company and U.S. Air Force sustainment/supply-chain workflows
cases.status: Company-reported deployment in selected supply-chain functions, with expanded partnership
cases.slide_claim: GE Aerospace says it uses Palantir AIP across selected supply-chain functions. Agents automate repetitive work spanning fulfillment, sourcing, allocation, maintenance, repair, and customer service. A J85 sustainment pilot began in early 2024; the partnership expanded in March 2026.
operator_workflow: Coordinate fulfillment, sourcing, and maintenance work
cases.agentic_evidence: GE's announcement explicitly describes deployed agentic AI and agents facilitating manual-task automation.
cases.boundary: No agent-specific quantified readiness gain or controlled evaluation is given. The release does not establish that the 2024 pilot was itself agentic or that agents authorize safety-critical engine maintenance.

cases.title: GE Vernova + Alabama Power: grid orchestration foundation
cases.us_relevance: Alabama utility serving 1.5 million customers; U.S.-headquartered grid technology vendor
cases.status: Operational automation / AI foundation; not verified LLM-agentic control
cases.slide_claim: GE Vernova's GridOS for Distribution unifies ADMS, DER management, network models, field work, and visual intelligence. Alabama Power is an early adopter. The vendor release reports over 112 million customer-minutes of interruption avoided in 2025 by the platform.
operator_workflow: Maintain governed network and operational data
Coordinate operations, field work, and DERs
Expose selected tools and records to a future agent layer
cases.agentic_evidence: The release describes operator-first AI, predictive analytics, and automation, but does not identify an LLM agent deployment at Alabama Power.
cases.boundary: Teach this as the trusted operational substrate agents can use. Do not attribute the 112-million-minute benefit to generative or agentic AI.

cases.title: Duke Energy: AI scam detection
cases.status: Deployed AI; agentic architecture not established by source
cases.slide_claim: Duke Energy deployed AI to scan websites, social media, and paid advertisements for scams targeting customers. It flags fake ads and impostor helplines for removal; Duke cites a recent takedown of a fake paid-search customer-service ad.
cases.agentic_evidence: Source verifies active AI use but does not specify LLM planning, tool use, or multi-agent orchestration.
cases.boundary: A useful adjacent-AI example. Any agentic extension shown in the tutorial must be labeled illustrative, not Duke's disclosed architecture.

cases.title: Siemens Eigen Engineering Agent + U.S. Prism Systems
cases.us_relevance: Siemens names U.S.-based automation integrator Prism Systems as a pilot customer
cases.status: Named U.S. customer pilot; product generally available from April 20, 2026
cases.slide_claim: Siemens launched the Eigen Engineering Agent after pilots with over 100 companies in 19 countries. U.S.-based Prism Systems used it to create, modify, and import SCL automation code in seconds. The agent connects to TIA Portal, executes multistep tasks, validates outputs, and iterates before engineer review.
operator_workflow: Agent reads project blocks, parameters, and relationships
cases.agentic_evidence: Official release specifies multistep reasoning, self-correction, execution, and validation against project requirements.
cases.boundary: This is automation engineering, not live plant control. 'In seconds' describes the reported Prism workflow, not a universal productivity guarantee.

cases.title: EPRI Open Power AI + SAFERai.power
cases.organization: Electric Power Research Institute and consortium members
cases.us_relevance: Palo Alto-based research organization; members include Duke, PG&E, Exelon, Southern Company, TVA, NYPA, and others
cases.status: Collaborative research, sandbox validation, and risk-framework initiative; not a utility production deployment
cases.slide_claim: EPRI's Open Power AI Consortium develops power-sector models, data, and sandbox applications. SAFERai.power, announced August 6, 2026, is developing an operational risk framework and assessment toolkit. Its autonomy guidance spans advisory use, supervised action, guarded autonomy, and exceptional autonomous use.
operator_workflow: Document data, permissions, model limitations, and oversight
cases.agentic_evidence: SAFERai explicitly addresses agentic autonomy, write authority, and operating reach.
cases.boundary: Do not call the consortium a deployed agent or imply that the proposed assessment toolkit and v1.0 deliverables are complete. Membership alone does not establish production use.

cases.title: Schneider Electric Resource Advisor+ and Sera
cases.us_relevance: Energy management company with substantial U.S. business; initial initiative announced in Boston, but launch source names no U.S. customer deployment
cases.status: Commercial product launch; named U.S. customer outcomes not established
cases.slide_claim: Schneider Electric launched Resource Advisor+ on January 20, 2026. Sera is a lead agent coordinating specialized agents over energy and sustainability data. The launch began with Carbon Performance and Supply Chain products; other capabilities were described as later additions.
operator_workflow: Interpret a sustainability or energy-management request
cases.agentic_evidence: Official launch identifies lead-agent orchestration and a network of agentic capabilities.
cases.boundary: A product case, not verified autonomous utility operations. Do not label all announced future modules generally available as of the launch date.

editorial_rules: Keep each source's derived narrative below 200 words across slides, speaker notes, and memo where feasible.
Use source references at the bottom of each case slide.
Label tutorial-designed workflows as illustrative rather than attributing undisclosed architecture to a company.
Preserve distinction between GE Aerospace and GE Vernova.
Do not represent production assistant workflows as autonomous physical grid control.
